description.value: The study tested whether increased frequency of social interaction acts as a social reward and whether reward-system activation is modulated by individual preferences for social interaction.

design.value: A within-subjects functional magnetic resonance imaging study in which participants completed a virtual ball-toss game and a button-press control task, each containing normal-frequency and high-frequency conditions.

description.value: A 14-item scale that measures allocentric tendency. Each item is rated on a five-point scale ranging from 1 “not at all” to 5 “very much”.
Participants rated how much they enjoyed the prior ball-toss or button-press block using a VAS ranging from 0 to 100, where 0 indicated “not at all” and 100 indicated “very much”.
Handedness was assessed according to the Edinburgh handedness inventory.

source_definition.value: Higher collectivism scores indicate high allocentric traits in social interaction, which are associated with higher affiliative tendency and higher sensitivity to rejection.

description.value: Thirty-eight adults (21 males and 17 females) took part in the experiment.

inclusion_criteria.value: All participants had normal or corrected-to-normal visual acuity, were right-handed according to the Edinburgh handedness inventory, and were free of neurological and medical disorders.

exclusion_criteria.value: One participant did not appear to follow the instructions, because she reported the same enjoyment ratings (100) under all conditions. In addition, six participants did not believe the task deception.

medical_condition.value: free of neurological and medical disorders

description.value: Data were analyzed from the remaining 31 participants (16 males, 15 females).

task_description.value: Participants played a virtual ball-toss game with four same-gender players that were unknown to them. Each run included six ball-toss blocks, six rating blocks, and six rest blocks.

instructions.value: Participants were told that they would be playing a virtual ball-toss game in an fMRI scanner along with four players located in a remote experimental room.

stimuli.value: Photographs of four virtual players and the participant were placed at the vertices of a regular pentagon. Participants tossed a ball to one of the other four virtual players.

task_description.value: Participants pressed a button according to the visual cues. The button-press run included six button-press blocks, six rating blocks, and six rest blocks.

instructions.value: Participants were required to press a button according to the following rules. O=“button press” and X=“no button press”.

stimuli.value: Button-press cues (O=“button press” and X=“no button press”) appeared at the center of the screen.

instrument.value: 3T scanner (Verio; Siemens, Ltd., Erlangen); 32-element phased-array head coil

description.value: fMRI was performed using an EPI gradient-echo sequence.
Whole-brain high-resolution, T1-weighted anatomical MRI using magnetization prepared rapid acquisition gradient echo (MP-RAGE) was performed for each participant.

The first four volumes of each fMRI run were discarded. Motion correction, slice-timing correction, co-registration, normalization to the MNI template, resampling, and spatial smoothing were performed.

steps.value: The first four volumes of each fMRI run were discarded because the MRI signal was unsteady.
Fourier phase-shift interpolation was used to correct the slice timing of each image to the middle slice.
The mean of the realigned EPI images was co-registered with the T1-weighted MP-RAGE image.
The co-registered T1-weighted MP-RAGE image was normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template using linear and nonlinear three-dimensional (3D) transformations.
The parameters from this normalization process were applied to each of the EPI images.
The anatomically normalized EPI images were resampled to a voxel size of 2mm×2mm×2mm.
Spatially smoothed using a Gaussian kernel of 8mm full width at half-maximum (FWHM).

model_settings.value: Five regressors were defined: ball-toss normal-frequency, ball-toss high-frequency, button-press normal-frequency, button-press high-frequency, and rating blocks. The general linear model included the six motion parameters and a constant term. Task regressors lasted 30s and the rating regressor lasted 5s.

estimator.value: random-effects analysis at the group level; paired t test

model_settings.value: Stepwise multiple regression was conducted between the collectivism scores and the average beta values related to high-frequency effects within 13-mm diameter spheres located at the peaks of significant clusters.

description.value: In the normal-frequency condition, each participant had six ball tosses during a block; in the button-press task there were six button-presses per block.
In the high-frequency condition, the number of ball tosses from each participant was 13 per block; in the button-press task there were 13 button-presses per block.
Participants played a virtual ball-toss game with four other virtual players.
Participants were required to press a button when “O” appeared and not press when “X” appeared.

role.value: greater side of the task comparison
lesser side of the task comparison

model_representation_notes.value: The general linear model included the six motion parameters and a constant term.

interpretations.value: The higher frequency of social interaction was represented as a social reward.

definition.value: experience effects were calculated as (experience [high-frequency enjoyment - normal-frequency enjoyment] - expectation [high-frequency enjoyment - normal-frequency enjoyment]) for the two runs (ball-toss and button-press).

interpretations.value: Participants reported greater-than-anticipated enjoyment during the high-frequency condition.
